ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier ('CMF'), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-58 (anti-money laundering and financing of terrorism obligations); Code de commerce, Articles L.123-23 and R.123-187 to R.123-190 (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs 'RBE'); Décret n° 2021-1627 du 10 décembre 2021 (RBE procedures); Ordonnance n° 2016-1408 du 20 octobre 2016; Loi n° 2018-700 du 3 août 2018; Arrêté du 27 janvier 2021 (standard form of UBO declaration); applicable FATF Recommendations and EU AML Directives 2015/849, 2018/843 and Regulation (EU) 2018/1673.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the beneficial owner's country of residence, with apostille/consular legalization as applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention 1961 (France: apostille issued by the competent authority of the State of origin; for non-Hague states, French consular legalization at the Consulate General of France)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, not older than 3 months) of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or account-holding bank in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If notarized or certified, Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; otherwise sworn French translation by a translator officially registered on the French court list

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent registry extract of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar or competent authority of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, plus sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter of the shareholder or UBO (anti-money laundering provenance of funds letter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding financial institution of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for the physical person executing the SAS articles of association and filing documents in France
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the country of origin of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by French sworn translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory negative screening of every shareholder, UBO and officer against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, French national asset-freeze files (FSCIN/Direction générale du Trésor), and the FATF High-Risk Jurisdictions list. The onboarding file must record screening date, screening engine reference, and match rationale. Because the business accepts USDC (cryptocurrency), additional EDD on the source of crypto funds and on the ownership of the receiving wallet is recommended; the standard French AML risk classification is Low_Risk_Standard for this ISIC scope.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; name and trademark collision verification via the INPI database at data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the exclusive language of official acts (Article 2 of the 1958 French Constitution; Loi n° 94-665 du 4 août 1994 'Loi Toubon'). The proposed corporate name must use Latin script; the statutes and all filings must be drafted in French. The name must be preceded or followed by the exact legal-form mention 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' or the initials 'SAS' and the share capital amount (Code de commerce, L.227-9 and R.123-237).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Banquier / Crédit (prior ACPR authorization required)
Assurance / Mutuelle / Assureur (prior ACPR authorization required)
Fonds d'investissement / OPCVM / FCPI (prior AMF authorization required)
Préfecture / Ministère / République / État / Cour / Tribunal (misleading public authority terms)
Université / Académie / École (misleading academic title; prior ministry consent)
Commune / Département / Région (geographic official denominations when misleading)
Third-party registered trademarks or well-known marks without proof of consent
Legal-form confusion tokens such as 'SA', 'SARL', 'SCA' when the entity is not of that form
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the INPI or the registry rejects the proposed name through the Guichet Unique, the applicant may (i) amend the name and re-submit online without additional statutory fee; (ii) file a hierarchical administrative recourse with the Directeur Général de l'INPI within 2 months of notification, attaching the full rejection notice and argued distinctiveness; and (iii) appeal the administrative decision before the Tribunal Judiciaire de Paris. If the rejection is issued by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce at the RCS registration stage, the applicant must bring a summary appeal before the Président du Tribunal Judiciaire exercising commercial jurisdiction within 15 days of the notification.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted under Article L.123-11-3 of the Code de commerce: an SAS may domicile its registered office with a licensed commercial domiciliation provider ('centre de domiciliation') for a renewable one-year minimum contractual term, provided the provider holds a commercial lease and is declared with the registry. Virtual office acceptance for this ISIC 6201 AI/LLM API business is high because no physical retail presence or licensed operational premises are required; this does not diminish the obligation to keep statutory books and records at the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-negligible; estimated 10-15% annual probability of unannounced verification of premises and records when a third-party domiciliation provider is used, based on inspectorate activity under Article L.123-11-4 of the Code de commerce. The risk increases if the domiciliation center aggregates a disproportionate number of registrations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: EUR 36.75 (approx. USD 40) standard registration duty

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-30 and R. 227-1 et seq. governing the Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS); Article L. 210-2 (nationality); Articles L. 225-218 et seq. (special provisions applicable to simplified companies); Code civil Article 1841 et seq. for corporate constitution.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of the Tribunal de Commerce having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic filings are made through the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises, operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declarative incorporation file lodged via the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), comprising the signed Articles of Association (statuts), the INSEE company creation data set, the legal notice publication certificate, the capital deposit certificate, and the beneficial owner declaration; the resulting official registration proof is the K-bis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital under Article L. 227-2 of the Code de commerce; shareholders may fix nominal capital as low as EUR 1. All cash contributions must be fully paid upon constitution and deposited with a French credit institution, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notary as depositary; the written depositary certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) must be attached to the Articles at the time of signature.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED unanimously at the founding meeting of [Company Name] SAS: the articles of association have been approved and the share capital of EUR [X], divided into [Y] ordinary shares, is hereby fully subscribed by the shareholders; all cash contributions have been deposited with the escrow bank and the depositary's certificate is acknowledged; the registered office is fixed at [Street, Postal Code, City], France; [Name] is appointed President of the Société par Actions Simplifiée, with all powers to represent and bind the company in dealings with third parties; the President is authorized to publish the legal notice, file the incorporation dossier through the Guichet Unique, sign all declarations, open bank and payment accounts, and appoint any executive officers as may be required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of cash capital and preparation of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution authorized by the ACPR, Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notary acting as depositary of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate bank account in the name of '[Company Name] SAS en formation' with a French bank; complete the bank's anti-money-laundering KYC questionnaire identifying every shareholder and beneficial owner; transfer or deposit the full agreed cash capital; obtain the bank's irrevocable certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt des fonds) stating the depositor, the company name, and the exact amount; retain the depositary account until the RCS registration certificate is issued. If a notary is used, execute the incorporation deed and have the capital deposited under notarial control.
required_dossiers: Draft of the Articles of Association (statuts)
Identity document (passport or national ID card) of each shareholder
Proof of residential address for each shareholder
Beneficial ownership information and declaration annex
Bank KYC and anti-money-laundering questionnaire
Identity document of the proposed President or corporate extract if the President is a legal entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the French bank refuses to open the account, invoke the right to a basic payment account under Article L. 312-1 of the French Monetary and Financial Code and request designation of an intermediary through the Banque de France; alternatively, deposit the capital with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or a notary, and resubmit the corrected KYC package within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Articles of Association and appointment of the President
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders acting collectively, assisted by a notary where preferred
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Articles of Association, checking the corporate name against INPI databases; include the corporate purpose covering generative artificial intelligence, large language model inference, and API platform services aligned with ISIC 6201 and APE code 6201Z; arrange physical or qualified electronic signature by each shareholder, with powers of attorney duly annexed; date the Articles and attach the bank's deposit certificate; simultaneously execute a written collective decision appointing the President of the SAS and any Director(s) of the President; obtain the President's signed acceptance of office.
required_dossiers: Final signed Articles of Association
Capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
Share subscription list and contribution valuation annex
Written collective decision appointing the President
Signed acceptance of office by the President
Certified copies of shareholders' identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Articles contain a legal or formal defect, cure it by executing a corrective collective shareholder decision or, where necessary, a notarial deed rectificatif confirming the content and re-dating the instrument; re-sign the corrected pages so the whole document forms a single coherent instrument before publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal incorporation notice in an authorized legal announcements journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorized for the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statutory legal notice (avis de constitution) containing the corporate form, corporate name, share capital, number of shares, corporate purpose, registered office address, duration, President's name, and the RCS court of registration; submit the notice to the selected journal by online transfer or email; pay the publication fee and request the journal's certificate of publication (attestation de parution); verify that the notice is published before the Guichet Unique filing and within one month following signature of the Articles.
required_dossiers: Text of the legal notice (avis de constitution)
Copy of the signed Articles of Association
Capital deposit certificate
Certificate of publication fee payment or purchase order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the journal rejects the notice due to formatting or content errors, resubmit a corrected notice in the same publication cycle and obtain a new attestation de parution; if the original notice has expired or becomes stale, arrange a fresh publication within the statutory validity window before filing with the Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the incorporation dossier to the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique operated by INPI at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; verified and registered by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in using FranceConnect+; select 'Création d'entreprise' and the legal form 'Société par Actions Simplifiée'; enter corporate data, registered office, activity, shareholders, President details, and beneficial owners; upload the signed Articles of Association, deposit certificate, legal publication certificate, registered office occupancy authorization, identity and residence proofs of the President and shareholders, the beneficial owner declaration, and the President's eligibility declaration; pay the greffe registration fee; monitor the application status through the Guichet Unique dashboard until validation or rejection.
required_dossiers: Guichet Unique online creation form data set
Signed Articles of Association
Certificate of legal notice publication (attestation de parution)
Capital deposit certificate
Registered office occupancy consent (bail or titre de jouissance)
Identity document and proof of address of the President
Beneficial owners declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
Declaration of eligibility and absence of convictions of the President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a rejection notice (bordereau de rejet), cure the identified deficiencies within the statutory 15-day cure period by uploading corrected or missing documents in the Guichet Unique application; if the second filing is refused, petition the judge supervising the RCS (juge commis à la surveillance du registre) for an order directing registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of K-bis extract, SIREN/SIRET identifiers, and activation of tax, employer, and payment circuits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS), INSEE, URSSAF, and the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, retrieve the official K-bis extract and the SIREN/SIRET identifiers; verify that URSSAF employer registration is automatically generated; apply to the local SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) for the intra-Community VAT number using form 1090 once the K-bis is available; provide the K-bis and corporate documents to Stripe for the merchant account; open a dedicated corporate wallet for USDC payments and adopt a written risk and AML policy consistent with the Low_Risk_Standard classification.
required_dossiers: K-bis registration extract
SIREN and SIRET assignment confirmation
Intra-Community VAT application for digital services
URSSAF employer registration data set
Corporate banking and payment-provider KYC pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis or SIRET identifiers are missing or erroneous, file a mise à jour request through the Guichet Unique and ask the Greffe for a rectified extract; if the intra-Community VAT number is delayed, file form 1090 directly with the SIE and request a written acknowledgement; if URSSAF registration is not auto-generated, enrol the company at urssaf.fr using the SIREN number.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sectoral industrial licensing board applies to dematerialized generative AI and LLM API platforms in France; horizontal digital-economy authorities are the Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE) and the Direction Générale de la Concurrence, de la Consommation et de la Répression des Fraudes (DGCCRF).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required under French law for the supply of AI/LLM API services; the RCS registration (K-bis) constitutes the sole pre-authorization for the business activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Inspection des Installations Classées — DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity generates no physical or industrial environmental exposure; no full EIA report and no environmental registration or authorization are required (Articles L. 122-1 et seq. of the Code de l'environnement are not triggered).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The API platform produces no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste. IT hardware must be managed under the French WEEE (DEEE) obligations of Articles L. 541-10-2 et seq. of the Code de l'environnement. Should the company later operate a data centre or server room, the installation may fall under ICPE Rubrique 2835-1 above 500 kW (déclaration) or Rubrique 2835-2 above 3 MW (autorisation), with applicable IED-emissions and refrigerant standards then becoming mandatory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil-defense fire certificate is required for purely office-based digital activity; the premises must nevertheless comply with workplace safety regulations of the Code du travail, including electrical installations checks, fire extinguisher maintenance, and emergency evacuation planning. If the company opens a customer-facing showroom or training space qualifying as an Établissement Recevant du Public (ERP), a fire safety commissioning checklist (commission de sécurité) and periodic controls apply under the Code de la construction et de l'habitation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), through the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official tax portal impots.gouv.fr. Business formation and statutory registration are filed through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is incorporated through the INPI Guichet unique. The filing generates the SIREN and SIRET identifiers and transmits the formation data to the DGFiP. The company must identify its competent SIE, provide its articles of association, registration extract, registered-office evidence, directors' and beneficial-owners information, business activity, bank details, and expected taxable turnover. The DGFiP assigns or confirms the corporate income-tax account and, where applicable, the French VAT identification number in the format FR plus a two-digit key and the nine-digit SIREN. VAT registration, intra-Community VAT activation, and filing-frequency requests are handled through the SIE and the relevant DGFiP forms and online services. A non-established foreign entity carrying out taxable French activities must register with the appropriate non-resident or local SIE before commencing transactions requiring French VAT compliance; an EU-established business may generally use the VAT One Stop Shop for eligible B2C intra-EU supplies, but the OSS does not replace a French VAT registration where French domestic taxable transactions, imports, stock, or other registration triggers exist.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) by default. A qualifying SAS may elect temporarily for income-tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu, IR), generally for a maximum of five financial years, if statutory conditions are satisfied, including qualifying ownership, business activity, size, age, and shareholder requirements. The election must be notified within the statutory period and is not a general check-the-box election. France does not provide a broad United States-style entity-classification election. Tax-transparent treatment may apply to qualifying partnerships or other legally distinct forms, but not automatically to an ordinary SAS. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement applicable EU and OECD-based limitations on deduction, exemption, and imported mismatch outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA), based on the European Union VAT Directive and French tax legislation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For French domestic businesses supplying services, the VAT franchise threshold is generally EUR 37,500 of prior-year turnover, with a current-year tolerance threshold of EUR 41,250, subject to statutory updates and sector-specific rules. The principal thresholds for goods and accommodation are generally EUR 85,000 and EUR 93,500. Exceeding the applicable threshold, electing for VAT, making transactions requiring registration, or conducting specified intra-Community or import transactions can trigger registration. Cross-border EU SME exemption rules may additionally require an EU-wide turnover limit of EUR 100,000 and compliance with the relevant national threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting for domestic B2B transactions. From 1 September 2026, all French businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices, and large enterprises and certain intermediate-sized enterprises must issue them; SMEs and micro-enterprises are generally subject to issuance from 1 September 2027. The timetable is subject to legislative implementation and permitted postponements. Invoices will be exchanged through an approved private platform or the designated public infrastructure, with structured data transmitted to the DGFiP. Transaction reporting (e-reporting) applies to relevant B2C and cross-border transactions. France does not generally require real-time pre-clearance of every invoice before issuance; digital transmission, structured-data compliance, authenticity, integrity, auditability, and reporting requirements apply. A service provider operating an AI API platform must retain valid invoice data and evidence of customer status, place of supply, VAT number, reverse-charge treatment, and export or out-of-scope treatment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with credit for input tax, provided the supplier establishes exportation and exit from the EU through customs records and transport evidence. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for exemption where the customer has a valid VAT number in another EU Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and the supplier satisfies recapitulative and evidentiary requirements. For AI inference, software, hosting, and API services, a B2B supply is generally located where the business customer is established or has the relevant fixed establishment; a supply to a customer established outside France is therefore commonly outside the scope of French VAT rather than a French zero-rated export. B2C digital services are generally taxed at the consumer's location and may require OSS or local registration. The supplier must verify customer status, contractual recipient, establishment, service nature, payment trail, and technical delivery evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration and customs exit confirmation, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN) or equivalent customs evidence
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and VAT treatment
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, airway bill, consignment note, carrier confirmation, or equivalent proof of dispatch and delivery outside the European Union
Packing list and, where applicable, import or destination customs documentation
Proof of contractual export responsibility and evidence linking the goods to the customs declaration
For intra-Community goods supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT identification number, transport evidence, and recapitulative statement records
For offshore or out-of-scope services, contract, customer establishment evidence, VAT-number validation where applicable, service-delivery records, invoices, and payment evidence
Bank payment and accounting records sufficient to reconcile the transaction; a separate inward-remittance certificate is not generally required under French law for ordinary export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation requirement for ordinary export receipts. Export VAT exemption is denied or clawed back where customs exit, transport, customer status, place of supply, or transaction records are insufficient. The DGFiP may assess unpaid VAT, applicable late-payment interest, and penalties; a 40% penalty may apply for deliberate failure or serious negligence, and an 80% penalty may apply for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of law, subject to statutory conditions. False invoices, fabricated export evidence, concealment, or intentional VAT fraud may also create criminal exposure, including fines and imprisonment under applicable law. Assessments generally include retrospective recovery for open tax years, and input VAT refunds may be rejected or recovered where the underlying zero-rating or taxable-business nexus is unsubstantiated. Records must be preserved for the applicable French tax and accounting retention periods and must be available in an auditable form.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) as the foreign-exchange policy authority and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the prudential and AML/CFT banking supervisor.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is part of the euro area and does not operate exchange controls for current or capital account transactions; currency convertibility is full and unrestricted in law, subject only to EU measures, financial sanctions, and anti-money-laundering procedures. The euro is freely convertible and cross-border payments in EUR, USD, GBP, and CHF can be made without prior central-bank approval. Profit remittance by a French SAS by way of dividends, management fees, or royalties is legally unrestricted, but in practice requires distributable profits, approved corporate accounts, a valid shareholder decision in the form required for an SAS, French tax residence evidence of the recipient, treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive analysis for withholding tax, and standard CRS/FATCA reporting by the paying bank. Capital contributions from non-resident shareholders are permitted without exchange approval and must be fully documented to satisfy KYC, balance-of-payments, and AML requirements. USDC stablecoin inflows are not subject to exchange control but attract enhanced due diligence and, where relevant, CASP licensing and MiCA compliance in the European Union.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France maintains no statutory surrender of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no forced repatriation timeline. A French SAS may receive foreign-currency export revenue into an authorized EU/EEA bank account or convert it into euros at any time. For balance-of-payments statistics, all cross-border transfers must pass through an authorized financial intermediary, and the SAS must provide the bank with correct transaction coding under the BPM6 service category applicable to computer services, cloud infrastructure, and API/LLM usage fees, together with any threshold-based REX declarations to the Banque de France. There is no obligation to invoice exports in a particular currency, but USD-invoiced AI/LLM API sales must be booked accurately for French VAT, CIT, and transfer-pricing purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is High for collecting digital API receivables through a licensed EU/EEA payment or e-money institution, Medium for using such institutions as the main treasury settlement account, and Low for a non-EEA offshore EMI as the primary banking layer. Stripe, operating through an EU payment-institution licence and passporting into France under PSD2, is a highly effective collection rail for AI/LLM token usage, card payments, and SEPA Direct Debit, but it is not a bank and does not provide deposit protection, capital escrow, FX hedging, or high-value trade settlement. Fully digital EU EMIs and neobanks may open accounts remotely with reasonable AML/KYC standards, but they impose lower transaction ceilings and are less suitable for large equity injections and intercompany treasury flows. A non-EEA offshore digital EMI established in the UK, Singapore, or the United States generally cannot lawfully provide payment accounts to a French resident without obtaining French or EU payment-service authorisation; any such arrangement requires a formal French regulatory legal opinion to prevent unlicensed payment activity under the French Monetary and Financial Code.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted under ACPR and AMF guidance where the customer completes a verifiable electronic identification procedure, including video KYC, digital identity verification, and electronic signature, and where all corporate documents are provided in notarized, apostilled, or officially endorsed form. In practice, Tier-1 French banks require a physical compliance interview for non-resident directors, significant shareholders, or UBOs when the account will hold capital escrow, support USDC-related treasury flows, or access FX lines. A remote-only onboarding route is viable through a digital EU bank or a PSD2-licensed EMI, but such accounts have lower limits and no bespoke corporate treasury services. The lowest-friction approach is to appoint a locally resident director or an authorized corporate signatory who can attend the KYC interview in France; a simple apostilled power of attorney is usually insufficient to replace the physical or video interview requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: USDC/stablecoin flows and crypto-adjacent settlement are treated as elevated ML/TF risk by French compliance teams, particularly because the platform advertises Cryptocurrency_USDC as a payment rail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written Treasury and Digital-Asset Policy; proof of the MiCA/CASP licence or ACPR/EU registration of the conversion platform; on-chain wallet ownership evidence and blockchain analytics reports demonstrating the source and destination of USDC; a board-approved procedure requiring immediate conversion of USDC into EUR and prohibiting third-party pass-through; transaction monitoring records; and a French legal memorandum confirming that the SAS is not itself a crypto-asset service provider and does not require CASP registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership and UBO opacity in an early-stage French SAS, combined with capital contributions from overseas shareholders and intercompany funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract; complete organigramme; authenticated passport and proof of address for each director and UBO holding more than 25%; French and foreign tax residence certificates; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; accountant-reviewed financial projections; shareholders’ agreement; capital call resolutions; French UBO register (RND) declaration; and professional or bank references for each ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border API customer traffic and metered billing patterns without an established client due-diligence file, creating perceived risk of platform abuse or third-party payment laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CFT institutional policy; customer risk-rating matrix; sanctions and PEP screening procedures; KYC files for enterprise API customers; terms of service that prohibit illegal or concealed payments; abuse-detection and traffic-monitoring controls; usage-metering and invoice-matching reports; and third-party PCI-DSS/GDPR compliance evidence for Stripe and other payment processors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AI model export-control, sanctions, or dual-use reputational exposure, where API users could include restricted end-users or jurisdictions subject to EU/UN/OFAC embargoes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Export-control and sanctions compliance manual; jurisdiction and end-user screening policy; API geo-blocking and IP-reputation controls; institutional customer onboarding procedure for high-risk accounts; outside counsel memo on dual-use classification of the LLM/API services; and a record of denied-party screening results before onboarding large institutional users.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All equity or intercompany funding from non-resident shareholders must be routed by SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer or SWIFT MT202 COV interbank cover into the French operating or capital-escrow account of the SAS at a Tier-1 bank. The payment message must reference the SIREN/SIRET identifier and the corporate purpose, such as subscription of new shares, capital increase, or shareholders’ current account. The bank will classify the flow for Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting as direct investment equity, other investment, or intercompany loan, and the SAS must contemporaneously file the shareholder resolution, capital-increase deed, subscription receipt, UBO declaration, CRS/FATCA self-certifications, and source-of-funds evidence. To avoid French tax re-characterization, all received amounts must be posted to the correct share-capital, share-premium, or shareholders’ current-account ledger and reported consistently to the French tax administration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payments to non-resident suppliers, contractors, and shareholders, the primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 customer transfers for high-value or cross-currency disbursements, SEPA Credit Transfers for EUR-denominated payments within the EU/EEA, and SWIFT MT202 COV for interbank cover of large instructions. Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600, documentary collections, and bank payment obligations are acceptable for physical hardware, data-centre equipment, and infrastructure purchases; digital service and API supplier fees may be settled through card acquiring via Stripe, SEPA Direct Debit, or SWIFT. All outbound payments must be supported by invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, and, where relevant, VAT or Intra-EU reporting; dividend distributions require evidence of distributable reserves, approval of the shareholders, and the correct French withholding-tax treatment. The bank will screen each disbursement against sanctions and PEP lists and may decline transfers to virtual-asset addresses, so USDC supplier payments should be minimized and executed only through a licensed EU CASP after documented conversion.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forwards with an ACPR-licensed French or EU credit institution
EUR/USD OTC FX options and zero-premium collars to protect the USD-denominated AI API revenue surplus
Cross-currency swaps for long-term intercompany loans between the French SAS and non-resident group treasury
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted currencies such as CNY and INR where local currency delivery is legally unavailable
FX swaps to manage short-term treasury mismatches between USD collections, EUR operating costs, and capital-call timing
Exchange-traded EUR/USD futures cleared through a recognized central counterparty and reported under EMIR

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing (dépôt des comptes annuels et annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the INPI guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within 6 months of fiscal year-end, then filing within 1 month of approval; practical deadline 31 July following a 31 December year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to €1,500 (natural person) / €3,000 (legal entity); court-ordered filing (injonction de faire) under Article L611-2 C. Com.; persistent default enables public prosecutor petition and administrative strike-off (radiation) after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, Cerfa 2065 series)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second business day after 1 May for calendar-year-end companies (5 May 2025 for FY 2024); within 3 months of year-end for non-calendar fiscal years.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge on unpaid tax (40% bad faith, 80% concealment) plus monthly 0.20% late interest; €150 minimum administrative penalty when no tax is due.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quarterly corporate income tax prepayments (acomptes d'IS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December of the tax year; balance settled with the annual return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Flat 5% late-payment penalty on unpaid instalment plus 0.20% monthly interest on the shortfall.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business contribution (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises - CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP on behalf of the commune / EPCI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual establishment declaration (n°1447-C) by 3 May for the following tax year; final CFE payment by 15 December of the tax year (or within 10 working days after formal notice); first-year entities are exempt for the year of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge plus 0.20% monthly interest and enforced treasury recovery; unpaid CFE for two consecutive years supports commercial-registry strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO beneficial-owner declaration maintenance and update (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via INPI guichet unique)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No standalone annual deadline; mandatory update within 30 days of any shareholding or control change (e.g., transfer exceeding 25% of capital or voting rights) and maintained accurate at each annual accounts filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to €7,500 (natural person) / €37,500 (legal entity) and up to 6 months imprisonment for deliberate omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT return (CA3) - monthly or quarterly, plus annual summary where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly CA3 due by the 19th of the following month (24th for e-filing with online payment); quarterly CA3 available to eligible SMEs, due by the 19th of the month following the quarter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-filing/payment surcharge (40% bad faith, 80% concealment) plus 0.20% monthly late interest; repeat defaults trigger tax-lien enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Social security filings (DSN - Déclaration Sociale Nominative)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly, by the 5th of the month following the payroll month (or 15th under the extended payroll-calendar option).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% late-payment surcharge on contributions plus 0.20% monthly interest; flat per-employee per-month fine for late or missing DSN filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial-registry renewal fee (droit annuel de greffe) keeping the K-bis extract current
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via INPI guichet unique)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual invoice issued by the Greffe in Q1-Q2, payable within 30 days of issue.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid fee blocks issuance of K-bis extracts and all registry operations; persistent non-payment combined with other registry defaults leads to administrative strike-off after formal notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) if any two of the following thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive fiscal years (Decree 2023-455, applicable from 1 January 2024): balance-sheet total > €6 million; net turnover > €12 million; average number of employees > 50. Mandatory irrespective of thresholds for SAS parent companies whose controlled group exceeds the same figures, upon judicial order, or when shareholders representing at least 1/3 of the capital petition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP - Plan Comptable Général (ANC Regulation 2014-03, in force as amended); EU-adopted IFRS permitted for voluntary consolidated statements but not required for an unlisted stand-alone SAS; annual accounts (balance sheet, P&L, notes) must be prepared in French and filed in euros.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France imposes no separate annual UBO re-filing. Beneficial owners are declared at incorporation and re-declared at the Greffe within 30 days of any change in shareholding or control; the Greffe automatically verifies the UBO statement at each annual accounts deposit and at each capital-related filing. Every transfer of shares or voting rights exceeding 25% of capital requires an updated UBO declaration within 30 days of the transfer.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$100-US$350 per year for a commercial domiciliation; US$600-US$2,200 per year for a full registered-office plus corporate-secretarial service provider.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable below the statutory thresholds; when a mandatory audit exists: US$4,500-US$13,000 per year (regional accountancy firm) or US$8,500-US$32,000 per year (national / Big Four firm).
